meta.notes: All data fetched directly from gametime.com product pages on 2026-10-24 (site allowed automated fetches; no dealer or cached sources were needed). Each component url is the page the values came from. GameTime product pages publish: Model Number, list price, Use Zone (Length x Width) in ft-in and m, Age Ranges, Fall Height, Suggested Number of Users, Weight and Material Specifications. They do NOT publish overall equipment footprint or overall height for most items, so footprint_in and height_in are null unless the size is in the product name or spec: for shade structures footprint_in is the canopy plan size from the model name (e.g. 20x20 ft = 240x240 in; the third number in the name is entry/clearance height, not overall height); PlayCurb dims come from its spec block. Overall dimensions are in the per-product CAD (.dwg) and SketchUp downloads linked on each page. usezone_in is GameTime's published use zone converted to inches with w = first number (published as Length) and d = second (Width); orientation relative to the equipment is not stated on the page. Use zone is null where the page omits it (most swing frames and seats, deck-attached slides/climbers/panels whose use zone is part of the host structure). fall_height_in is GameTime's published Fall Height; where GameTime lists "Deck Height" (deck-attached components) the value is null and the note says it equals the host deck height. A published 0' fall height is kept as 0. capacity is the max of GameTime's "Suggested Number of Users" figure; for swing frames and seats GameTime's figure appears to be a playground-capacity planning number (e.g. 25-30 for one swing frame), not riders at once, so treat with care. Some amenity pages show placeholder values (e.g. Bench "35 to 40", Rectangular Hip Shade "1"); those were nulled. ages mapping: GameTime "2 to 5 Years" -> 2-5, "5 to 12 Years" -> 5-12, both -> 2-12, "13+ Years" -> 13+. Site furnishings with no age range are tagged 13+ (adult/general use); shade canopies with no age range are tagged 2-12 (placed over play areas); Dome Boulder has no published age (null). Tot's Toddle Rocker is 6-23 months on GameTime but placed in 2-5 because the schema has no under-2 bucket. ada field is a planner classification derived from GameTime's own wording (ramp, transfer height, ground-level/zero-entry, inclusive) - GameTime does not publish a per-item ADA category; null means GameTime did not state an accessibility feature on the page. Prices are GameTime list prices shown on the site on 2026-10-24 (before freight, installation, surfacing, tax, rep/co-op discounts such as Sourcewell/OMNIA contracts); play-system pages show no price. STANDARDS cited on gametime.com/resources/certifications: ASTM F1487 (Standard Consumer Safety Performance Specification for Playground Equipment for Public Use) - GameTime products conform and GameTime staff sit on the ASTM committee; CPSC Public Playground Safety Handbook (Pub. #325) recommended for owners/operators; IPEMA third-party equipment certification to ASTM F1487 and CSA CAN/CSA Z614; IPEMA surfacing certification of GT Impax to ASTM F1292 (impact attenuation of surfacing); ADA - DOJ 2010 ADA Standards for public playgrounds (accessible routes, surfacing, transfer, ground-level components; GameTime publishes an ADA compliance checklist and states all pre-designed PowerScape Plus and PrimeTime plans meet accessibility guidelines); TUV SUD America testing to the European harmonized standard (EN 1176); ISO 9001, ISO 14001 (Fort Payne, AL plant), PCI 4000 powder-coat certification. GT Impax PIP page states it meets all ASTM standards applicable to playground safety surfaces and ADA guidelines. NOT found cited on gametime.com pages checked: ASTM F2223 and the specific ADA sections 240 / 1008 by number (GameTime refers generically to DOJ ADA playground standards and the U.S. Access Board) - planners should still apply ADA 2010 Standards 240 (play areas: ground-level/elevated component counts, 1:2 ramp/transfer rules) and 1008 (play-area accessible routes, transfer systems, ground surfaces per ASTM F1951/F1292). For Forest, MS planning: use zones published here already include ASTM F1487/CPSC clearance; (per ASTM F1487/CPSC, to-fro swing use zones extend 2x pivot height front and rear). Compliance must still be verified with the GameTime rep (Forest, MS area) and the stamped CAD/use-zone drawing for each final layout.

lines.name: PrimeTime
lines.notes: GameTime's value line: smaller uprights and decks than PowerScape, more compact designs needing less safety surfacing and lower cost; patented TruLoc DirectBolt connections (no clamps). Full themed accessory set (climbers, toppers, panels, roofs). PrimeTime swing frames use 3-1/2" O.D. x .120" galvanized posts. Pre-designed systems carry PT model prefixes (e.g. PT24144). Exact PrimeTime upright O.D. and deck module size were not published on the pages checked. Conversion Deck (19900) joins PrimeTime to PowerScape.

lines.name: PowerScape
lines.notes: High-capacity line: "industry-leading 49 inch deck" - 49" center-to-center upright spacing; square (80000) and triangle (80001) punched-steel decks, PVC coated, min 2,381 sq in, bolted with eight 3/8" cap screws. PowerScape swing frames 5" O.D. x .120" galvanized. Roof options seen: Angled Hoop Roof, ShadowPlay acrylic tree roofs, 8-post integrated fabric shade (square/hex deck, 2- or 3-deck span). Pre-designed systems carry PS prefixes.

lines.name: Xscape
lines.notes: Modular, obstacle-course style play for 2-5 (balance/strength) and older kids; integrates with PE programs; climbing walls such as DNA Climbing Wall; angled Xscape swing frames (3-1/2" x 7', two seats per bay). Pre-designed systems carry XS prefixes.

lines.name: Modern City
lines.notes: X-Frame hub with cast-aluminum shrouds; uprights double as climbing routes; multi-tiered (ground, mid, upper) play with open sight lines. Modern City swing frame uses 5" x 5" square uprights; Saucer Swing.

components.notes: Wear mat for swing/slide-exit high-wear zones in loose fill. See top-level surfacing list for full notes. List price on gametime.com $336 (Oct 2026).

surfacing.name: GT Impax Poured In Place (PIP) Rubber (model PIP1)
surfacing.notes: 2-layer: 1/2" rubber wear course hand-troweled over custom-depth attenuation layer sized to fall height. Granules standard 1-4 mm or premium 0.5-1.5 mm; aliphatic binder; urethane topcoats available. Sub-base: concrete, asphalt or compacted aggregate; install at 40-45 F minimum. Meets ADA and applicable ASTM surfacing standards. Maintenance: debris removal, roll coats, preventive maintenance at least every 18 months; TPV inserts recommended at swing/slide exits. Supports graphics and mounds. https://www.gametime.com/poured-in-place-rubber

surfacing.name: GT Impax Bonded Rubber (RecycledBonded1)
surfacing.notes: Single-layer recycled rubber + binder poured over sub-base (concrete, asphalt, compacted aggregate); 7 solid colors or specialty mix; EPDM inlays possible; 100% US recycled; good for natural look and walking paths. https://www.gametime.com/recycled-bonded-rubber

surfacing.name: GT Impax Interlocking Tiles (RecycledTiles1)
surfacing.notes: Patented interlocking rubber tiles, unitary stable surface; various colors/thicknesses; made in USA from recycled rubber. Sub-base: concrete or asphalt with drainage. Best on flat, high-traffic, accessible areas. https://www.gametime.com/recycled-rubber-tiles

surfacing.name: GT Impax Synthetic Turf (Turf1)
surfacing.notes: Tufted synthetic grass over compliant attenuation layer; multiple blade heights; sub-base concrete, asphalt or compacted aggregate; no mowing. https://www.gametime.com/turf

surfacing.name: Engineered Wood Fiber (EWF1)
surfacing.notes: Loose-fill wood fiber; approved attenuation up to 12 ft fall height; knits into a surface that supports wheelchairs/walkers when maintained; sub-base compacted earth with drainage; must be topped up often to stay compliant. Lowest initial cost. https://www.gametime.com/engineered-wood-fiber

surfacing.name: Loose Fill Rubber (RecycledLoose1)
surfacing.notes: Recycled-tire rubber mulch (US recycled), more color options; best for higher fall heights; mold/insect resistant, does not freeze; sub-base compacted earth with drainage; needs refills; pair with wear mats. https://www.gametime.com/recycled-loose-fill-rubber

surfacing.name: Wear Mats (161292)
surfacing.notes: Black mats (85% recycled rubber, 15% EPDM, polyurethane binder) placed on top of or just below loose fill under swings and slide exits to reduce displacement and maintenance. https://www.gametime.com/wear-mats-161292
